results.root_cause_actual: PR #881 raised the payments-svc read timeout from 3s to 30s and disabled the circuit breaker. When partner acquirer latency spiked to 12.4s p99, payment threads held connections open for up to 30s (exceeding the ALB's 10s proxy_read_timeout, causing edge 504s) and exhausted the 64-thread shared pool, blocking all routes including those unrelated to payments.
results.root_cause_expected: PR #881 raised the gateway's payments-svc read timeout from 3s to 30s (and disabled the circuit breaker) while the edge load balancer's proxy_read_timeout stayed at 10s. When partner latency rose, the edge cut clients off at 10s with 504s while gateway worker threads stayed pinned on the upstream call for the full 30s, saturating the 64-thread pool and taking down routes that never touch payments-svc.

judge.reason: Both identify the same underlying cause: PR #881's timeout mismatch between gateway (30s) and edge load balancer (10s), combined with disabled circuit breaker, allowing payment threads to hold resources for the full 30s and exhaust the shared thread pool when upstream latency increased.

evidence_cited: PAYMENTS_CIRCUIT_BREAKER  enabled -> disabled  (breaker tripped too often at 3s)
